html:
In 897 a scholar from Medina, Yahya ibn al-Husayn, called al-Hadi ila'l-Haqq, came to Saada in northern Yemen to settle tribal feuds and founded the Zaydi imamate. Imams of his line ruled parts of Yemen, on and off, until 1962.

Zaydis are a branch of Shia Islam close to Sunni practice. They held that any learned descendant of Ali who rose against injustice could claim the imamate. The imams' power rested on the tribes of the northern highlands, and it rose and fell with them.

The last imams ruled the Kingdom of Yemen until the revolution of 1962. The Houthi movement, from the same Saada region, draws on this Zaydi past in the war since 2014.
